title: orch ticket v1
description: One ticket = one file .orch/tickets/<id>.json. Writers must produce valid tickets. Unknown fields are allowed everywhere (top level and nested) and every reader/writer keeps them unchanged. Every field added after the first release is optional, so older tickets stay valid. The core knows no add-on: add-on data lives only under ext.<add-on name> and is checked by that add-on's own schema (addon-manifest.md, ticket_ext). type and wake_at are gone: wait until a time with waiting_on {kind: time, until}; recurrence is add-on data under ext.

id.description: Random, e.g. t_7k3f9q. Same as the file name.

revision.description: +1 on every write. `orch ticket patch --if-revision N` is refused when it changed (no lost updates between agents and add-ons). Missing = 0.

waiting_on.description: Generic waiting. The core records it and never promises that something wakes the ticket (an add-on may). kind time needs until; the other kinds need ref.

ref.description: question: q1 · ticket: t_… · external: ws_…, wh_…, a person, a PR URL, free text

ext.description: One key per add-on (its manifest name) or tool. Each owner decides its own shape; an installed add-on's ticket_ext schema checks its key on every write. Others never change a key they do not own.

owner.description: Optional. The person who owns the ticket, free text (a name), e.g. 'Severin'. Not a login.

due.description: Optional. Due day, YYYY-MM-DD, no time and no zone.

note.description: Optional. Free note from people, shown on the ticket. Plain text.

summary.description: Optional. Where things stand, one or two plain sentences, kept current by whoever works on it. Used to start a fresh agent session.

parent.description: Optional. Id of the parent ticket (sub-tickets). Set at creation. Children are not stored on the parent: they are found by reading every ticket's parent.

sessions.description: Optional. Agent sessions that worked on this ticket, one entry per agent and machine (host). A new run resumes the entry whose agent and host match; otherwise it starts fresh. No age limit. The gitignored run record (run.schema.json) holds only the claim.

who.description: agent:<adapter name> (e.g. agent:my-agent) or human:<name>. Add-ons that write log as agent:<add-on name>.

ref.description: PR URL, commit hash, file path (a copied file lives in the gitignored .orch/tickets/<id>/evidence/), URL, the command line, or the note text

title.description: Optional short name shown instead of ref.

role.description: Optional. result = what was asked for; check = proof it works; support = anything else.

state.description: Optional. 'doing' = someone works on this item now (by, at say who and since when). Absent = not started or done (see done).

check.description: Evidence-based: done=true needs at least one evidence entry.

type.description: Any tool: github, jira, teams, file, ticket, ...

via.description: Where the answer came from (free word, e.g. cli, web, phone). null while unanswered.

kind.description: Optional. plain (default) or <add-on>:<name>; the add-on with that prefix acts on the answer. The core only records it.

action.description: Optional, opaque to the core: data the asking add-on needs to act on the answer.

check.description: Optional. The checklist item this question belongs to.

via.description: Optional. Surface the change came from (free word).

token.description: A short free word (a-z, 0-9, -) naming the surface or channel, e.g. cli, web, phone. The core never lists the allowed values.

agent_name.description: An agent adapter name: a key of agents.json or a [agents.<name>] table in .orch/config.toml.

id.description: The agent tool's own session id.

host.description: Machine name where the session lives; resume only on the same host.
